=={{header|Omegese}}==
{{works with|omc|sha256 2c824805, aien-dev/omega-mv e5b32567, Linux AArch64}}
Omega has no imports, so the small output helpers (<code>emit</code> and friends) are part of the program.
<syntaxhighlight lang="text">
om2
text nl "\n"
text sp " "
text minus "-"
text data "12 -4 7 88 0 31 -4 56 23 9 -70 45 2"
global vals long 16
note emit writes every byte of a to stdout; a short write is retried, an error exits 1
fn emit a view uchar * to void
o = ulong 0
while lt o len a bound 4096
k = write 1 a o sub len a o
if le k 0
exit 1
end
o = add o ulong k
end
end
note emitu writes n in decimal; 20 digits hold every ulong
fn emitu n ulong to void
d = new uchar 20 0
i = ulong 20
v = n
while true bound 20
i = sub i 1
put d i uchar add rem v 10 48
v = div v 10
if eq v 0
break
end
end
emit part d i sub 20 i
end
note emiti writes a signed n; the magnitude is taken as a ulong so the minimum long cannot overflow
fn emiti n long to void
if lt n 0
emit minus
emitu add bitcast ulong not n 1
else
emitu ulong n
end
end
note parse reads the decimal numbers in s (separated by spaces, an optional - sign) into vals and
note returns how many; one pass over s, so the loop is bounded by len s
fn parse s view uchar * to ulong
n = ulong 0
v = long 0
sg = long 1
dig = false
for i ulong len s
c = get s i
if eq c 45
sg = long -1
else
if and ge c 48 le c 57
v = add mul v 10 long sub c 48
dig = true
else
if dig
put vals n mul sg v
n = add n 1
end
v = long 0
sg = long 1
dig = false
end
end
end
if dig
put vals n mul sg v
n = add n 1
end
ret n
end
note show writes vals[0..n-1] separated by spaces, then a newline
fn show n ulong to void
for i ulong n
if gt i 0
emit sp
end
emiti get vals i
end
emit nl
end
note sift moves vals[s] down the max-heap vals[0..n-1]; r at least doubles each pass, so 16 passes suffice
fn sift s ulong n ulong to void
r = s
while lt add mul r 2 1 n bound 16
c = add mul r 2 1
if lt add c 1 n
if lt get vals c get vals add c 1
c = add c 1
end
end
if ge get vals r get vals c
ret
end
t = get vals r
put vals r get vals c
put vals c t
r = c
end
end
note hsort heapifies bottom-up, then swaps the maximum to the end n-1 times
fn hsort n ulong to void
s = shr n 1
while gt s 0 bound 16
s = sub s 1
sift s n
end
e = n
while gt e 1 bound 16
e = sub e 1
t = get vals 0
put vals 0 get vals e
put vals e t
sift 0 e
end
end
fn main to int
n = parse data
show n
hsort n
show n
ret 0
end
</syntaxhighlight>
{{out}}

12 -4 7 88 0 31 -4 56 23 9 -70 45 2
-70 -4 -4 0 2 7 9 12 23 31 45 56 88
</pre>
